parole.significato: alms (something given to the poor as charity, such as money, clothing or food)
parole.testo: From Slovene almužna, from Late Latin eleēmosyna (“alms”), from Ancient Greek ἐλεημοσύνη (eleēmosúnē, “pity, mercy”). Doublet of elemózsia.

parole.significato: cabbage (an edible plant having a head of green leaves)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Slovene or Slovak. Compare Slovak kapusta.

parole.significato: birdlime (a sticky substance smeared on branches to catch birds)

parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Slovene. Compare Slovene mládec (“young man”) (plural mládci, which may be the direct source of the Hungarian form), mladič (“young animal”), and mlad (“young”). Compare also Serbo-Croatian mládac, mlàdīć. For sense 3, compare German Schwein haben (“to have a swine/to be lucky

parole.significato: nase (any fish of the genus Chondrostoma)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Slovene podust. First attested in the c. 1600.

parole.significato: brushwood, twig, stick (dry branches and twigs fallen from trees and shrubs)
parole.testo: From Slovene rožje (“cuttings from vine shoot”).

parole.significato: bit (a piece of metal placed in a horse's mouth and connected to the reins to direct the animal)
